terms.name: Aadhaar
terms.description: India's national digital identity programme; Aadhaar verifiable credentials are issued as ISO 18013-5 mdoc credentials under UIDAI.

terms.name: Access Certificate
terms.description: A certificate for electronic seals or signatures that authenticates and validates a (Wallet-)Relying Party, issued by a provider of access certificates; governed by ETSI TS 119 411-8 (RP Access Certificate Policy).

terms.name: Access Certificate Authority
terms.description: A provider mandated by a Member State to issue Relying Party access certificates to (wallet-)relying parties registered in that Member State.

terms.name: Accreditation
terms.description: The formal recognition that an assessment or certification body is competent to perform specific conformity assessment activities within a defined scope.

terms.name: ACDC
terms.description: Authentic Chained Data Container (KERI-related) credential representation; used notably in the GLEIF vLEI credential family.

terms.name: ACDC Schema
terms.description: Schema in the ACDC / KERI family for chained authentic data.

terms.name: Administrative validity period
terms.description: The date(s) from and/or up to which the attributes in a PID or attestation are valid, represented as attributes in the attestation (some attestations, such as diplomas, have none).

terms.name: Age Verification Credential
terms.description: A verifiable credential used to prove that a holder meets a minimum age threshold without revealing full identity, common in age-restricted access scenarios.

terms.name: Agentic AI
terms.description: Credentials intended for agentic AI or automated agent contexts (for example machine-readable delegation or service identity). Rare in current catalogs; reserved for emerging use cases.

terms.name: Agriculture
terms.description: Farming, agrifood production, and rural economy.

terms.name: AnonCreds
terms.description: Privacy-preserving format using zero-knowledge proofs for selective disclosure without correlatable identifiers.

terms.name: Apple Wallet Pass
terms.description: Apple's pass format for storing credentials, tickets, and keys in the Wallet app on iOS and macOS.

terms.name: APTITUDE
terms.description: An EU Large Scale Pilot consortium testing EUDI Wallet use cases in mobility, transport, and banking, including digital travel documents and strong authentication for digital payments.

terms.name: Attestation
terms.description: In the EUDI Wallet context, a collective term for a QEAA, PuB-EAA, or (non-qualified) EAA that can be stored in and presented from a Wallet Unit. Not the same as a UNTP Conformity Attestation (supply chain conformity assessment).

terms.name: Attestation Provider
terms.description: In the EUDI Wallet context, a collective term for a QEAA, PuB-EAA, or EAA Provider that issues wallet attestations. For UNTP conformity issuers, see Conformity Assessment Body.

terms.name: Attestation Revocation List
terms.description: A mechanism that communicates the revocation status of PIDs and attestations by publishing a list of identifiers of revoked items.

terms.name: Attestation Rulebook
terms.description: A document describing an attestation type, its namespace(s) and other features for a specific attestation type.

terms.name: Attestation Status List
terms.description: A mechanism that communicates the revocation status of PIDs and attestations by publishing Valid or Invalid status information for all relevant items.

terms.name: Attestation Type
terms.description: An identifier for a type of attestation, unique within the context of the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

terms.name: Attribute
terms.description: A characteristic, quality, right or permission of a natural or legal person or of an object, carried inside a PID or attestation.

terms.name: Authentic Source
terms.description: A repository or system, under the responsibility of a public or private body, that is the primary or recognized source of attributes about a person or object.

terms.name: Authority
terms.description: The organization or body responsible for defining and governing the credential type (schema, rules, and trust framework).

terms.name: Availability
terms.description: Whether the wallet is generally available to users or still in development.

terms.name: BBS+
terms.description: Signature scheme supporting selective disclosure and unlinkable proofs; used in some privacy-preserving credential systems.

terms.name: Beneficial Ownership Registers Interconnection System
terms.description: An EU system interconnecting national beneficial ownership registers under the Anti-Money Laundering framework, using EUID identifiers; complementary to business register data in wallet contexts.

terms.name: Beta-ID
terms.description: Swiss Beta-ID personal identity credential issued through the swiyu Beta Credential Service, carrying core identity attributes and derived age proofs in SD-JWT VC format.

terms.name: Bitstring Status List
terms.description: Compact status list where each credential maps to a bit; used for revocation and suspension checks.

terms.name: Boarding Pass Credential
terms.description: A digital boarding pass credential representing a passenger's entitlement to board a specific flight, used in IATA contactless travel flows.

terms.name: Booking Order Credential
terms.description: A digital travel credential representing a flight reservation or booking order in contactless travel scenarios.

terms.name: Both
terms.description: The Relying Party supports both the Proximity Flow and the Remote Flow (user and device physically near the RP in some scenarios, and interaction over the internet from different locations in others).

terms.name: Business Registers Interconnection System
terms.description: An EU system interconnecting national business registers, using the European Unique Identifier (EUID) to identify companies across Member States; linked to European Business Wallet identity data.

terms.name: Capabilities
terms.description: What business wallets can do: store credentials (holder), issue new credentials (issuer), or verify credentials from others (verifier).

terms.name: Certificate Authority
terms.description: An entity trusted by one or more parties in the ecosystem to create and seal certificates.

terms.name: Certificate of Residence
terms.description: A verifiable credential attesting a person's place of residence, used in EUDI Wallet flows for address verification and compliance with residence-based entitlements.

terms.name: Certification
terms.description: The formal attestation that a product, service, system, process, organization, or claim has successfully demonstrated conformance with the requirements of a certification scheme or assessment programme.

terms.name: Certification Body
terms.description: A conformity assessment body authorized to issue certifications or certificates based on the results of conformity assessments. A certification body may perform assessments itself or rely on assessment results produced within its accredited scope.

terms.name: Certification Scheme
terms.description: A defined set of rules, requirements, assessment criteria, governance processes, and assurance mechanisms used to evaluate and certify conformance.

terms.name: Client to Authenticator Protocol
terms.description: Protocol between a client (browser or OS) and an authenticator device; pairs with WebAuthn for hardware-backed user authentication.

terms.name: Compliance Reporting
terms.description: Credentials used for regulatory compliance, tax, customs, conformity, or official reporting workflows.

terms.name: Comprehensive Learner Record
terms.description: A standard for verifiable digital records of learning achievements and competencies, complementary to Open Badges in education ecosystems.

terms.name: Conformity Assessment
terms.description: The process of evaluating whether specified requirements have been fulfilled by a product, service, system, process, organization, or claim. In UNTP, a conformity assessment is a specific measured evaluation against a criterion, recorded in a Digital Conformity Credential.

terms.name: Conformity Assessment Body
terms.description: An organization that assesses whether products, services, systems, processes, organizations, or claims conform to the requirements of a specific scheme, standard, trust framework, or conformity assessment program. In UNTP, CABs issue Digital Conformity Credentials.

terms.name: Conformity Attestation
terms.description: In the UNTP context, a conformity attestation issued by a competent body that defines one or more assessments about a product or facility against a standard or regulation; the subject of a Digital Conformity Credential. Not the same as an EUDI Wallet attestation (EAA/QEAA/PuB-EAA).

terms.name: Conformity Profile
terms.description: In the UNTP context, a versioned scope of audit under a conformity scheme, composing one or more criterion and defining the subject type (product, facility, or organisation).

terms.name: Conformity Scheme
terms.description: In the UNTP context, a formal governance framework under which conformity attestations are issued, published as a versioned linked-data vocabulary in the Conformity Vocabulary Catalog.

terms.name: Conformity Topic
terms.description: A UNTP standard classification for what is being assessed (for example emissions, forced labour, or water usage), used to align criterion and assessments across schemes.

terms.name: Conformity Vocabulary Catalog
terms.description: The UNTP mechanism for scheme owners to publish conformity schemes, profiles, and criterion as machine-readable linked-data vocabularies so DPP claims can be verified against DCC assessments.

terms.name: Construction
terms.description: Built environment, construction sites, and infrastructure projects.

terms.name: Core minimum functionalities
terms.description: The minimum interoperable set of European Business Wallet functions that public sector bodies must accept: identification/authentication, signing/sealing, and submission/receipt of documents and official notifications.

terms.name: COSE
terms.description: Binary signature format optimized for constrained devices and bandwidth efficiency.

terms.name: Country
terms.description: Country where the provider is based.

terms.name: Credential Format
terms.description: The technical format in which credentials are encoded. Different formats support different features like selective disclosure, privacy protection, or compatibility with specific standards.

terms.name: Credential Issuer Metadata
terms.description: OpenID4VCI discovery document at a credential issuer's well-known endpoint describing supported credential types, formats, and cryptographic parameters.

terms.name: Credential Offer
terms.description: An OpenID4VCI object by which an issuer offers one or more credentials to a wallet, initiating the issuance flow.

terms.name: Credential Status
terms.description: How the validity of credentials is checked: whether they are revoked, suspended, or still valid. Different methods use different technical approaches.

terms.name: Credential Theme
terms.description: Cross-sector use-case themes for discovering credential types (for example identity, payments, or trade documents). Themes complement sector and ecosystem tags and describe why a credential might be used, not only which industry it belongs to.

terms.name: Criterion
terms.description: In the UNTP context, a specific auditable rule within a conformity scheme or standard (for example a carbon-intensity calculation rule), identified by a unique URI and referenced in claims and assessments.

terms.name: Data Space
terms.description: A governed ecosystem where organisations share data under agreed rules; Gaia-X credentials commonly attest participant identity, resources, and compliance in data spaces.

terms.name: Dataset
terms.description: The credential is issued about a dataset or data collection.

terms.name: Dataspaces
terms.description: Credentials used in data space, federation, or trusted data sharing scenarios beyond a single application.

terms.name: Decentralised Access Control
terms.description: The UNTP specification defining access-control patterns that balance transparency with confidentiality when sharing supply chain credentials, from anonymous public access to decentralised authentication.

terms.name: Decentralized Identifier
terms.description: A self-controlled, resolvable identifier that does not depend on a central registry; the basis for DID methods such as did:web and did:key.

terms.name: Deferred Credential Issuance
terms.description: An OpenID4VCI pattern where the wallet receives a transaction reference first and fetches the credential later once the issuer has prepared it.

terms.name: did:ebsi
terms.description: DID method for the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure; used in EU digital identity contexts.

terms.name: did:jwk
terms.description: DID method embedding a public key directly in the identifier; self-contained without external resolution.

terms.name: did:key
terms.description: DID method where the identifier is derived from a public key; compact and self-certifying.

terms.name: did:peer
terms.description: DID method for peer-to-peer relationships; often used in direct connections between two parties.

terms.name: did:web
terms.description: DID method using web domains; DID document hosted at a URL leveraging existing domain reputation and TLS security.

terms.name: did:webvh
terms.description: DID method with verifiable history; extends did:web with version control and cryptographic proof of document history.

terms.name: DIDComm v1
terms.description: Earlier version of the DIDComm secure messaging protocol for communication between entities with DIDs.

terms.name: DIDComm v2
terms.description: Secure messaging protocol for DID-based communication; used for agent-to-agent credential exchange and notifications.

terms.name: Digital
terms.description: Digital services, ICT, and online platforms when no more specific sector applies.

terms.name: Digital Conformity Credential
terms.description: A UNTP verifiable credential issued by a conformity assessment body (CAB) providing independent, digitally verifiable assessment of a product, facility, or organisation against published standards or regulations.

terms.name: Digital Credentials API
terms.description: A browser and operating-system API that lets websites and apps invoke a wallet to request and present digital credentials.

terms.name: Digital Credentials Query Language
terms.description: A query language used in OpenID4VP that lets a verifier describe exactly which credentials and claims it requests from a wallet.

terms.name: Digital Facility Record
terms.description: A UNTP verifiable credential issued by a facility owner describing facility identity, location, ownership, and sustainability performance over a reporting period.

terms.key: Digital Identification and Authentication Council of Canada
terms.name: Digital Identification and Authentication Council of Canada
terms.description: Canadian non-profit coalition advancing digital trust and identity; develops and maintains the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework (PCTF).

terms.name: Digital Identity Anchor
terms.description: A UNTP verifiable credential issued by an authoritative register that binds a decentralised identifier (DID) to a registered identity (for example a VAT number or business register entry).

terms.name: Digital Product Passport
terms.description: A UNTP verifiable credential issued by a shipper carrying product identity, characteristics, and sustainability performance for serialised products or batches. Not the same as the EU regulatory Digital Product Passport (ESPR), though related in purpose.

terms.name: Digital Product Passports
terms.description: Credentials linked to product passports, sustainability, or supply-chain traceability. Includes UNTP Digital Product Passports (verifiable credentials) as well as EU regulatory DPP contexts.

terms.name: Digital Traceability Event
terms.description: A UNTP verifiable credential recording a product lifecycle activity (make, move, or modify) in a value chain, linking products to facilities and enabling upstream traceability.

terms.name: DIIP v4
terms.description: Community-driven interoperability profile based on OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP combined with DIDs, VCDM 2.0 and SD-JWT VC credentials.

terms.name: DIIP v5
terms.description: Community-driven interoperability profile based on OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP 1.0 versions combined with DIDs, VCDM 2.0 and SD-JWT VC credentials.

terms.name: Document
terms.description: The credential is issued about a document or formal record.

terms.name: Document Identifiers
terms.description: Document identifiers define which standardized document types this organization can exchange (e.g. invoice, credit note, order). Defined by national, international, or domain-specific standards, these machine-readable identifiers enable systems to recognize and process the documents correctly. Examples include Peppol UBL Invoice and Credit Note 2.0, and UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice and Credit Note (D22A).

terms.name: EAA and PID Profiles
terms.description: ETSI technical specifications defining general, presentation, and issuance requirements for Person Identification Data and Electronic Attestations of Attributes in the EUDI Wallet (ETSI TS 119 472 parts 1–3).

terms.name: EBWOID
terms.description: European Business Wallet Owner ID: a verifiable credential carrying an organization's identity attributes, issued via OpenID4VCI for use in European Business Wallet workflows.

terms.name: ECDSA ES256
terms.description: Elliptic curve signature algorithm providing strong security with efficient key sizes.

terms.name: Economic operator
terms.description: Any natural or legal person, or entity conducting economic activity, that may use a European Business Wallet to interact with public authorities or other businesses.

terms.name: Ecosystem
terms.description: A broad interoperability or policy context a credential type is associated with (for example the EUDI Wallet ecosystem, UN/CEFACT trade data, or Gaia-X). Used to discover credentials that fit a given stack or programme.

terms.name: EdDSA
terms.description: Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm; modern signature scheme (e.g. Ed25519) with fast verification.

terms.name: Education
terms.description: Schools, universities, training providers, and qualifications. As a sector tag it classifies the credential’s industry; as a theme tag it highlights education-related use cases (for example diplomas or student ID).

terms.name: eIDAS
terms.description: The EU Regulation (No 910/2014) on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market.

terms.name: Electronic Attestation of Attributes
terms.description: An attestation in electronic form that allows attributes of a person or object to be authenticated. The general building block alongside PID.

terms.name: Electronic Seal
terms.description: Data in electronic form attached to or logically associated with other data to ensure the latter's origin and integrity; used by a legal person.

terms.name: Electronic Signatures and Infrastructures
terms.description: ETSI technical committee suite (ESI) specifying trust services, qualified signatures, certificate profiles, and related protocols underpinning eIDAS and the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

terms.name: Embedded Disclosure Policy
terms.description: A set of rules embedded in an attestation by its provider that indicates the conditions a relying party must meet to access the attestation.

terms.name: Employee ID Credential
terms.description: A verifiable credential identifying an employee and their association with an employer, used in workforce and access-management scenarios.

terms.name: Endorsement
terms.description: In the UNTP context, the authority under which a conformity scheme or assessment is issued (for example accreditation of a test lab by a national authority).

terms.name: Energy
terms.description: Utilities, power, renewables, and energy markets.

terms.name: Engagement Context Role
terms.description: A vLEI credential expressing a context-specific business role in an engagement, such as supplier, buyer, customer, or auditor.

terms.name: ES384
terms.description: ECDSA with P-384 curve; stronger variant of ES256 for signatures and key agreement.

terms.name: ES512
terms.description: ECDSA with P-521 curve; higher security level elliptic curve signature algorithm.

terms.name: EU Attestation Catalog
terms.description: The set of standardized EUDI Wallet attestation and credential types defined by the European Commission and Large Scale Pilots (for example EHIC, PDA1, CoR, and PoR), published as schemas and rulebooks for interoperable issuance and presentation.

terms.name: EU Company Certificate
terms.description: A digital certificate attesting company information for use in cross-border business procedures, intended for use within European Business Wallets under the EU 28th regime framework.

terms.name: EUDI Certificate Profiles
terms.description: ETSI certificate profile requirements for PID Providers, Wallet Providers, Attestation Providers, and related EUDI actors (ETSI TS 119 412-6).

terms.name: EUDI Wallet
terms.description: European Digital Identity Wallet context: credential types aligned with the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework and related specifications.

terms.name: EUDI Wallet ARF
terms.description: EUDI Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework defining requirements and guidance for interoperable EUDI Wallets.

terms.name: EUDI Wallet Trust Mark
terms.description: A mark indicating that a wallet or service is a recognized, certified part of the European Digital Identity Wallet ecosystem.

terms.name: European Business Wallet
terms.description: A digital wallet for organizations, developed at EU level, that enables businesses and public sector bodies to identify themselves, manage mandates, exchange verifiable data, and interact securely across borders with full legal effect. A specialised form of an organizational wallet, built on the EUDI Wallet architecture.

terms.key: European Business Wallet Owner Identification Data
terms.name: European Business Wallet Owner Identification Data
terms.description: Identification data issued for an economic operator or public sector body that owns a European Business Wallet, used to verify identity and attributes in a business context.

terms.name: European Digital Directory
terms.description: A Commission-maintained directory of economic operators and public sector bodies using European Business Wallets, enabling trusted contact and identification across borders.

terms.name: European Digital Identity Regulation
terms.description: Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending eIDAS, which establishes the European Digital Identity Wallet framework. Commonly called eIDAS 2.

terms.name: European Digital Identity Wallet
terms.description: A digital wallet that enables individuals and organizations to securely store, manage, and share identity data, attributes, and credentials within the European Digital Identity ecosystem.

terms.name: European Diploma
terms.description: A verifiable credential representing a formal educational qualification or diploma issued in an EU context, for use in EUDI Wallet education and employment flows.

terms.name: European Health Insurance Card
terms.description: A verifiable credential representing the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC), used to prove entitlement to medically necessary healthcare during a temporary stay in another European country.

terms.name: European Social Security Pass
terms.description: An EU initiative and credential family for portable social security documents (notably PDA1 and PDA2) carried in the EUDI Wallet to support cross-border employment and social protection.

terms.name: European Unique Identifier
terms.description: A Union-wide unique identifier for companies and other legal entities, used in European Business Wallets where assigned under EU company law or anti-money-laundering rules.

terms.name: European Wallet Consortium
terms.description: An EU Large Scale Pilot consortium developing EUDI Wallet specifications, schemas, and conformance tooling. Publishes the EWC v3 interoperability profile.

terms.name: EWC v3
terms.description: European Wallet Consortium LSP interoperability profile with specification set and conformance approach targeting EUDI Wallet implementations. See also European Wallet Consortium (EWC).

terms.name: Facility
terms.description: In the UNTP context, a production or processing site (such as a factory, mine, or warehouse) whose identity and sustainability performance are described in a Digital Facility Record.

terms.name: FIDES
terms.description: FIDES means trust in Latin. The name was chosen for the FIDES Community to reflect the shared ambition of improving online trust through open collaboration, interoperable digital wallets, verifiable credentials, and related trust technologies. The community is guided by the principles of the FIDES Manifesto.

terms.name: FIDES Community
terms.description: An open community focused on improving online trust through interoperable digital wallets, verifiable credentials, trust ecosystems, and open collaboration. The community brings together public and private sector participants to accelerate trusted digital interactions based on the principles of the FIDES Manifesto. The community is supported by FIDES Labs.

terms.name: Finance
terms.description: Banking, insurance, payments, and financial services.

terms.name: Food
terms.description: Food safety, labeling, retail food, and agrifood distribution.

terms.name: Gaia-X
terms.description: Gaia-X and federated data infrastructure contexts where credentials may describe trust, compliance, or data space participation. See also Gaia-X (glossary).

terms.name: Gaia-X
terms.description: A European initiative for federated, interoperable data infrastructure where participants exchange data and services under common trust rules using verifiable credentials.

terms.name: Gaia-X Compliance Credential
terms.description: A Gaia-X verifiable credential attesting that a participant or service meets the Gaia-X Trust Framework requirements for a given compliance level.

terms.name: Gaia-X Federation Services
terms.description: Operational services that support Gaia-X federations, including compliance verification, identity management, and credential issuance infrastructure.

terms.name: Gaia-X Participant Credentials
terms.description: Gaia-X credential types describing legal participants: Legal Participant, Legal Registration Number, and Terms and Conditions credentials.

terms.name: Gaia-X Resource Credentials
terms.description: Gaia-X credential types describing federated assets and offerings: Resource, Service Offering, Data Resource, Physical Resource, and Software Resource credentials.

terms.name: Gaia-X Trust Framework
terms.description: The Gaia-X policy and technical rules defining how participants prove compliance, identity, and trustworthiness in federated data spaces.

terms.name: Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation
terms.description: The global authority that maintains the LEI system and governs the verifiable LEI (vLEI) credential framework for digital organizational identity.

terms.name: Google Wallet Pass
terms.description: Google's pass format for storing credentials and passes in the Google Wallet app on Android and the web.

terms.name: HAIP v1
terms.description: OpenID Foundation interoperability profile for high-assurance exchanges, including both SD-JWT VC and ISO mdoc vc formats. Will be used in EUDI-Wallet implementations.

terms.name: Health ID
terms.description: A verifiable credential carrying a person's health-related identifier for use in cross-border or digital healthcare contexts within the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

terms.name: Healthcare
terms.description: Health services, medical records, and patient-related credentials where applicable.

terms.name: Holder
terms.description: Can store and present credentials to verifiers (holder role).

terms.name: HSM
terms.description: Hardware Security Module; dedicated hardware for key storage and cryptographic operations, often used in servers.

terms.name: HTTPS ISS
terms.description: Issuer identified by HTTPS URL; credential issuer metadata and public keys retrieved from a web endpoint.

terms.name: IATA Contactless Travel
terms.description: IATA programme for digital travel credentials and contactless passenger flows using ISO mdoc credentials such as boarding passes and booking orders.

terms.name: IBAN Attestation
terms.description: A verifiable credential attesting a holder's International Bank Account Number (IBAN) and related account attributes for payment and financial onboarding use cases.

terms.name: Identifiers
terms.description: Methods for identifying issuers, holders, and verifiers in credential exchanges. Includes decentralized identifiers (DIDs), HTTPS URLs, OAuth client IDs, and X.509 certificates.

terms.name: Identity Resolver
terms.description: The UNTP specification defining how identifier systems (business registers, product registries, facility cadastres) support a consistent discover-resolve-verify workflow for supply chain identifiers.

terms.name: IETF Token Status List
terms.description: IETF mechanism for representing revocation and suspension status of credentials using token status lists; commonly used with SD-JWT VC credentials.

terms.name: Implementing Act
terms.description: A Commission Implementing Regulation that provides binding technical rules and specifications under the European Digital Identity Regulation.

terms.name: India Stack
terms.description: India Stack and related national digital infrastructure contexts where verifiable credentials are used. See also Aadhaar and UIDAI.

terms.name: Interaction Mode
terms.description: Determines how the holder interacts with the verifier.

terms.name: Intermediary
terms.description: A Relying Party that offers services to other (intermediated) Relying Parties to connect to Wallet Units and request user attributes on their behalf.

terms.name: Interop Profile
terms.description: Interoperability profiles define choices within existing standards and protocols that ensure wallets, issuers, and verifiers work together seamlessly across different implementations.

terms.name: ISO 18013-5
terms.description: International standard for mobile driver's licenses with device retrieval (local presentation).

terms.name: ISO 18013-5
terms.description: International standard for mobile driver's licenses with device retrieval (local presentation).

terms.name: ISO 18013-7
terms.description: Extension of ISO 18013-5 adding remote presentation capabilities for mobile driver's licenses over the internet.

terms.name: ISO 18013-7
terms.description: ISO standard for remote presentation of mobile documents including mDL; extends ISO 18013-5 proximity flows for internet-based verification.

terms.name: ISO Data Model
terms.description: Structure defined by an ISO standard data model (for example for mdoc types).

terms.name: ISO mDL
terms.description: ISO mobile document (mDL / mdoc) ecosystem: credentials based on ISO/IEC 18013-5 and related standards.

terms.name: ISO/IEC 23220
terms.description: ISO standard family for identity management via mobile devices, covering generic eID data objects and encoding rules referenced alongside mdoc in EUDI Wallet specifications.

terms.name: Issuance Protocol
terms.description: The protocol used to issue credentials from an issuer to a wallet. Defines how authentication, credential request, and delivery work.

terms.name: Issuer
terms.description: Can create and issue new credentials to users or businesses (issuer role).

terms.name: JAdES
terms.description: JSON Advanced Electronic Signatures; ETSI baseline format for signing JSON payloads, relevant alongside JOSE-secured credentials (ETSI TS 119 182-1).

terms.name: JOSE JWS
terms.description: JSON-based signature format for web applications providing integrity and authenticity.

terms.name: JSON-LD Context
terms.description: Schema or context expressed as JSON-LD for semantic interoperability.

terms.name: JSON-LD VC
terms.description: W3C VC format supporting rich semantic data with linked data capabilities.

terms.name: JWT Validity
terms.description: Credential status determined by JWT expiration timestamp.

terms.name: JWT-VC
terms.description: W3C credential format using JSON Web Tokens for signing and verification.

terms.name: Key Attestation
terms.description: A type of Wallet Unit Attestation that attests the certification and properties of a WSCA/WSCD or keystore and the public keys whose private keys it protects.

terms.name: Key Binding
terms.description: Cryptographic proof that the wallet holder controls the private key bound to a presented credential, preventing replay by another party.

terms.name: Key Storage
terms.description: Where cryptographic keys are stored: in secure hardware (like TPM or secure enclave) or in software (encrypted storage).

terms.name: Keystore
terms.description: A hardware-backed repository and service in which non-critical cryptographic keys are generated, stored and used inside a dedicated hardware security boundary (e.g. Secure Element, TPM, TEE, secure enclave, or remote HSM).

terms.name: Large Scale Pilot
terms.description: An EU-funded pilot consortium testing EUDI Wallet use cases across Member States. Examples include the European Wallet Consortium (EWC) and POTENTIAL.

terms.name: Legal Entity Identifier
terms.description: A globally unique 20-character code identifying a legal entity in financial and trade transactions; the basis for vLEI credentials.

terms.name: Legal equivalence
terms.description: The principle that actions performed through a European Business Wallet have the same legal effect as equivalent actions in person, on paper, or via other established processes.

terms.name: Legal person
terms.description: A legal entity such as a company, association, or public body, as distinct from a natural person (an individual human being).

terms.name: Legal Person Identification Data
terms.description: A set of standardized identity attributes that establishes the identity of a legal person (such as a company). The organizational counterpart to Person Identification Data (PID) in business wallet ecosystems.

terms.name: License
terms.description: Software license type: open source (publicly available code) or proprietary (closed source).

terms.name: Lifecycle Event
terms.description: In the UNTP context, a product lifecycle activity recorded as a Digital Traceability Event, modelled as a make, move, or modify event.

terms.name: List of Trusted Entities
terms.description: A list of entities recognized as trustworthy within a given approval scheme for a specific scope or purpose (based on ETSI TS 119 602).

terms.name: Make Event
terms.description: A UNTP traceability event type recording manufacturing or production of a product at a facility.

terms.name: Mandate
terms.description: A digital authorization that lets one person act on behalf of an organization within defined limits; a core European Business Wallet capability for delegation.

terms.name: Manufacturing
terms.description: Production, industrial goods, and factory-related processes.

terms.name: mDL/mDoc
terms.description: ISO (18013-5) binary (CBOR) format for mobile documents with strong authentication and selective disclosure. See also Mobile Driving Licence Credential for the mDL use case.

terms.name: mdoc
terms.description: ISO (18013-5 style) mobile document encoding (CBOR/COSE), often used for mDL and similar credentials.

terms.name: Member State
terms.description: A country of the European Union, obligated under the European Digital Identity Regulation to offer at least one EUDI Wallet to its citizens and residents.

terms.name: ML-DSA (FIPS 204)
terms.description: Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard; NIST post-quantum signature algorithm.

terms.name: Mobile Document Type
terms.description: A docType string identifying an ISO mdoc credential type in MSO mdoc issuance and presentation (for example eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1).

terms.name: Mobile Driving Licence Credential
terms.description: An ISO/IEC 18013-5 mobile driving licence (mDL) credential carried as an MSO mdoc; used for identity and driving entitlement verification.

terms.name: Mobility
terms.description: Transport, automotive, maritime, aviation, and traveller-related use cases.

terms.name: Modify Event
terms.description: A UNTP traceability event type recording modification or transformation of a product at a facility.

terms.name: Move Event
terms.description: A UNTP traceability event type recording movement of a product between facilities or locations in the supply chain.

terms.name: MSISDN Attestation
terms.description: A verifiable credential attesting a holder's mobile phone number (MSISDN) for identity binding, authentication, or contact verification.

terms.name: Namespace
terms.description: A specification of the attribute identifiers, syntax and semantics of attributes that can be used in an attestation, with an identifier unique within the ecosystem.

terms.name: National Accreditation Body
terms.description: An organization responsible for accrediting conformity assessment bodies and other assessment organizations against defined competence and impartiality requirements within a jurisdiction.

terms.name: National Cybersecurity Certification Authority
terms.description: A national authority responsible for overseeing cybersecurity certification schemes, supervising certification activities, and coordinating national implementation of cybersecurity certification frameworks.

terms.name: OAuth 2.0
terms.description: The authorization framework underlying OpenID Connect and OpenID4VC; governs how wallets, issuers, and verifiers obtain and delegate access tokens during credential flows.

terms.name: Official Organizational Role
terms.description: A vLEI credential linking a person to a formal role within a legal entity, such as CEO, director, or board member.

terms.name: Once-Only Technical System
terms.description: A cross-border data exchange system that enables competent authorities to retrieve evidence directly from authoritative sources, reducing the need for citizens and organizations to repeatedly submit the same information.

terms.name: Open Badges
terms.description: Open Badges and open recognition ecosystems for education, training, and achievement credentials. See also Open Badges 3.0 and Comprehensive Learner Record (CLR).

terms.name: Open Badges 3.0
terms.description: The current Open Badges standard for issuing and verifying digital badges and learning achievements, aligned with verifiable credentials practices.

terms.name: Open Source
terms.description: Source code is publicly available; licensing (e.g. Apache, MIT) defines use and distribution.

terms.name: OpenID Client ID
terms.description: OAuth 2.0 client identifier used in OpenID4VC flows to identify wallets and applications in authorization.

terms.name: OpenID Connect
terms.description: An identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0; OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP build on OpenID Connect patterns for wallet issuance and presentation flows.

terms.name: OpenID Identity Assurance
terms.description: OpenID Connect extension for conveying verified identity claims and assurance levels; referenced in EUDI Wallet identity proofing and issuer metadata contexts.

terms.name: OpenID4VCI
terms.description: OpenID-based protocol for securely issuing credentials to wallets.

terms.name: OpenID4VP
terms.description: OpenID-based protocol for requesting and presenting credentials to verifiers.

terms.name: Organization
terms.description: The credential is issued about a legal entity such as a company, association, or government body.

terms.name: Organizational
terms.description: Wallet for businesses and organizations to issue, hold, or verify credentials in professional contexts. Filter value for organizational/business wallets; see also Organizational Wallet and European Business Wallet.

terms.name: Organizational Identity
terms.description: Credentials about organizations: legal identity, roles, registrations, VAT, or business identifiers.

terms.name: Organizational Wallet
terms.description: A digital wallet used by organizations to issue, hold, and verify credentials. Often called a business wallet; broader than the EU-regulated European Business Wallet product.

terms.name: Other
terms.description: Credential format not covered by the standard formats listed in the catalog.

terms.name: Other
terms.description: Other or proprietary schema specification type.

terms.name: PAdES
terms.description: PDF Advanced Electronic Signatures; ETSI baseline format for signing PDF documents with the wallet (ETSI EN 319 142-1).

terms.name: Pan-Canadian Trust Framework
terms.description: A Canadian digital identity trust framework developed by DIACC, defining components such as digital wallets, verified persons, and privacy requirements.

terms.name: Party
terms.description: In the UNTP context, an organisation involved in a supply chain (manufacturer, shipper, assessor, etc.), referenced across UNTP credentials to identify actors. Not the same as a Relying Party in the EUDI Wallet context.

terms.name: Payments
terms.description: Credentials supporting payment use cases (for example IBAN attestations, loyalty, or payment-wallet-related proofs).

terms.name: Peppol
terms.description: Pan-European network and standards for secure exchange of electronic documents such as e-invoices and orders between businesses and governments.

terms.name: Performance Claim
terms.description: In the UNTP context, a declaration in a Digital Product Passport or Digital Facility Record that a product or facility meets a specific criterion, which can be verified against an independent Digital Conformity Credential.

terms.name: Person
terms.description: The credential is issued about a natural person (individual human being).

terms.name: Person Identification Data
terms.description: A set of identity attributes, issued under EU or national law, that establishes the identity of a natural or legal person. Forms the foundational identity in the EUDI Wallet.

terms.name: Person Identity
terms.description: Credentials about natural-person identity, attributes, or eligibility (for example PID, age verification, or health identifiers).

terms.name: Personal
terms.description: Wallet for individuals to store and present their own credentials, such as ID cards or diplomas.

terms.name: Photo ID
terms.description: A verifiable credential carrying a holder's portrait and core identity attributes for visual identification, distinct from full PID or mDL credentials.

terms.name: PID Provider
terms.description: The party responsible for issuing and revoking Person Identification Data and for cryptographically binding it to a Wallet Unit.

terms.name: PKI Cert Validity
terms.description: Credential status verified through X.509 certificate validity periods.

terms.name: Platform
terms.description: Operating system or environment the wallet runs on (e.g. iOS (iPhone), Android, Web).

terms.name: Portable Document A1
terms.description: A verifiable credential representing the EU PDA1 certificate, proving that an employee remains covered by their home country's social security system when working across borders.

terms.name: Portable Document A2
terms.description: A verifiable credential representing the EU PDA2 certificate, used in cross-border social security contexts to document applicable legislation for posted workers or multi-state employment.

terms.name: POTENTIAL
terms.description: An EU Large Scale Pilot consortium testing EUDI Wallet use cases in mobility, transport, and banking, including digital travel documents and strong authentication for digital payments.

terms.name: Power of Attorney
terms.description: A formal authorization for one party to act on another's behalf in legal or administrative matters; a key use case for European Business Wallets and the EU digital PoA.

terms.name: Power of Representation
terms.description: An EUDI Wallet attestation documenting that a natural person is authorised to act on behalf of another person or organisation within defined limits. Not the same as a European Business Wallet Power of Attorney (PoA) or mandate.

terms.name: Pre-authorized Code
terms.description: An OpenID4VCI issuance flow where the holder scans a QR code or follows a link containing a pre-authorized code to receive credentials without a separate authorization step.

terms.name: Presentation Exchange
terms.description: A DIF specification format used to describe which credentials and claims a verifier requires and how a wallet should respond.

terms.name: Presentation Protocol
terms.description: The protocol used to present credentials from a wallet to a verifier. Defines how credential requests and presentations are exchanged.

terms.name: Process Identifiers
terms.description: While document identifiers define which document types this organization can exchange, process identifiers define how this organization processes and exchanges those documents. They represent standardized workflows that define how documents are handled and how messages are sequenced. Examples include Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 (used for invoices and credit notes), Peppol BIS Order 3.0, and UN/CEFACT Buy-Ship-Pay workflows.

terms.name: Product
terms.description: The credential is issued about a physical or digital product.

terms.name: Proprietary
terms.description: Closed-source software; the vendor retains full control over the code and distribution.

terms.name: Provider
terms.description: Whether the wallet or service is provided by government or private sector.

terms.name: Proximity
terms.description: The Proximity Flow is used when the user and their device are physically near the Relying Party.

terms.name: PS256
terms.description: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256; RSA signature algorithm with probabilistic padding for signing.

terms.name: Pseudonym
terms.description: Data uniquely representing a user that, in itself, does not allow inferring the user's attributes or identity without additional information held separately by the issuer.

terms.name: Public Sector
terms.description: Government and public administration: public services, e-government, and official issuers.

terms.name: Public Sector Body EAA
terms.description: An Electronic Attestation of Attributes issued by, or on behalf of, a public sector body responsible for an authentic source.

terms.name: Qualified Electronic Attestation of Attributes
terms.description: An Electronic Attestation of Attributes issued by a Qualified Trust Service Provider and meeting the requirements of Annex V of the European Digital Identity Regulation.

terms.name: Qualified Electronic Registered Delivery Service
terms.description: A qualified trust service that transmits data between third parties by electronic means and provides evidence on the handling of the data, including proof of delivery; offered alongside European Business Wallets.

terms.name: Qualified Electronic Seal
terms.description: An advanced electronic seal created with a qualified seal creation device and based on a qualified certificate; legally ensures origin and integrity of data for a legal person.

terms.name: Qualified Electronic Signature
terms.description: An advanced electronic signature created with a qualified signature creation device and based on a qualified certificate; legally equivalent to a handwritten signature.

terms.name: Qualified Electronic Signature Creation Device
terms.description: Configured software or hardware used to create an electronic signature that meets the requirements of Annex II of the European Digital Identity Regulation.

terms.name: Qualified Trust Service Provider
terms.description: A trust service provider that has been granted qualified status under an applicable trust framework and is authorized to provide one or more qualified trust services.

terms.name: Qualified vLEI Issuer
terms.description: An organization authorized by GLEIF to issue vLEI credentials to legal entities and their representatives.

terms.name: Readiness
terms.description: Maturity or deployment stage of the relying party website (e.g. production, pilot).

terms.name: Registered Identity
terms.description: In the UNTP context, an identity as recorded in an authoritative register (such as a business or product registry), bound to a DID through a Digital Identity Anchor.

terms.name: Registrar
terms.description: The body designated by a Member State that establishes and maintains the list of registered wallet-relying parties in its territory.

terms.name: Relying Party
terms.description: A service provider that interacts with a Wallet Unit to request and receive user attributes (for example to authenticate a user or verify a credential).

terms.name: Relying Party Attributes
terms.description: Standardized information about a Relying Party shown to the user when deciding whether to share attributes, as specified in ETSI TS 119 475.

terms.name: Remote
terms.description: The Remote Flow is used when the user and the Relying Party are in different locations, and the interaction happens over the internet.

terms.name: Remote Presentation Protocol
terms.description: Protocol for remote (online) presentation of credentials, enabling verification over the internet without physical proximity.

terms.name: Remote Signature Protocols
terms.description: Protocols for creating qualified electronic signatures remotely via a cloud or server-side QSCD, including ETSI TS 119 432 and the Cloud Signature Consortium (CSC) API used in EUDI Wallet signing scenarios.

terms.name: Representation rights
terms.description: The rights of a natural person to act on behalf of a legal person or organization, managed digitally through mandates in business wallet contexts.

terms.name: Reservation Credential
terms.description: An ISO mobile document credential representing a reservation or booking entitlement, carried as an MSO mdoc.

terms.name: Retail
terms.description: Consumer retail, e-commerce, and point-of-sale contexts.

terms.name: RevocationList2020
terms.description: W3C status list format for credential revocation; each entry is a bit in a compressed bitstring.

terms.name: RP Access Certificate Policy
terms.description: ETSI policy for access certificates that authenticate Wallet Relying Parties, complementing the Access Certificate concept (ETSI TS 119 411-8).

terms.name: RS256
terms.description: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256; widely used RSA signature algorithm in JWT and certificates.

terms.name: Schema Type
terms.description: The kind of formal specification used to define the credential's structure (for example JSON Schema or an ISO data model).

terms.name: Scheme
terms.description: A defined framework of rules, requirements, governance, participants, and trust mechanisms that participants follow to achieve a specific purpose.

terms.name: Scheme Owner
terms.description: The organization responsible for defining, governing, maintaining, and evolving a scheme, including its requirements, policies, governance processes, and oversight mechanisms.

terms.name: SD-JWT-VC
terms.description: IETF SD-JWT-based verifiable credential format allowing holders to selectively reveal only necessary claims using salted hashes; builds on the core Selective Disclosure JWT (SD-JWT) specification.

terms.name: SD-JWT-VC
terms.description: IETF SD-JWT-based verifiable credential format with selective disclosure via salted hashes.

terms.name: Seafarer Credential
terms.description: A verifiable credential for maritime workers documenting seafarer identity, qualifications, or employment status in mobility and transport contexts.

terms.name: Sector
terms.description: Industry or domain. For relying parties: where the service operates. For credential types: which vertical the credential mainly applies to.

terms.name: Secure Enclave (iOS)
terms.description: Apple’s dedicated coprocessor for storing keys and performing crypto operations on iOS devices.

terms.name: Selective Disclosure
terms.description: The capability that enables a user to present only a subset of the attributes contained in a PID or attestation.

terms.name: Selective Disclosure JWT
terms.description: IETF format for JWTs with selectively disclosable claims using salted hashes; the cryptographic basis for SD-JWT VC credentials.

terms.name: Signature Algorithm
terms.description: Cryptographic algorithm used for signing credentials in this interoperability profile.

terms.name: Signature Scheme
terms.description: Signature encoding format: JOSE (JSON-based for web) or COSE (binary CBOR for constrained environments like embedded systems).

terms.name: Signing Algorithm
terms.description: Cryptographic algorithms used to sign credentials and presentations, ensuring authenticity and integrity.

terms.name: Single Digital Gateway
terms.description: An EU initiative requiring key public services to be accessible online across borders, complemented by European Business Wallets for trusted B2G identification and data exchange.

terms.name: SIOPv2
terms.description: Self-Issued OpenID Provider; allows the holder to act as an OpenID provider and present self-issued or other credentials.

terms.name: Software
terms.description: The credential is issued about a software application or system.

terms.name: Software Key Storage
terms.description: Keys stored in software (e.g. encrypted storage), without dedicated hardware protection.

terms.name: StatusList2021
terms.description: W3C status list encoding for revocation and suspension; used with Verifiable Credentials.

terms.name: Strong User Authentication
terms.description: Authentication based on at least two independent factors from different categories (knowledge, possession, inherence), designed so that compromise of one does not affect the others.

terms.name: StrongBox (Android)
terms.description: Android’s hardware-backed Keystore (StrongBox Keymaster) for key storage on supported devices.

terms.name: Subject Type
terms.description: The type of entity the credential is issued about: person, organization, product, dataset, software, or document.

terms.name: Supervisory Body
terms.description: An organization responsible for overseeing ongoing compliance with the requirements of a scheme, trust framework, or regulatory programme and for taking corrective or enforcement actions where necessary.

terms.name: Supply Chain
terms.description: Logistics, sourcing, traceability, and end-to-end supply chain operations.

terms.name: Supported Wallet
terms.description: Wallets that the relying party website has been tested with or supports.

terms.name: swiyu
terms.description: Swiss national digital identity programme (swiyu) and credential ecosystem, including the Beta-ID credential and swiyu interoperability profile.

terms.name: swiyu v0
terms.description: Swiss national digital identity interoperability profile (public beta) for SD-JWT VC credentials using OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP. Published by the swiyu (Swiss e-ID) programme.

terms.name: Tax Number Attestation
terms.description: A verifiable credential attesting a holder's tax identification number as registered with the relevant tax authority.

terms.name: Tax Residency Attestation
terms.description: A verifiable credential attesting a holder's tax residency status for cross-border tax and compliance workflows.

terms.name: Technical validity period
terms.description: The dates from and up to which an attestation is technically valid, represented as metadata; typically much shorter than the administrative validity period for privacy reasons.

terms.name: TEE
terms.description: Trusted Execution Environment; isolated area in the processor for running sensitive code and storing keys.

terms.name: Trade
terms.description: International and domestic trade, commerce, and marketplaces.

terms.name: Trade Documents
terms.description: Credentials representing trade and logistics documents such as invoices, bills of lading, or purchase orders.

terms.name: Transaction Code
terms.description: A user-facing code in OpenID4VP that the holder confirms to approve a presentation, providing explicit consent before credentials are shared.

terms.name: Trust Anchor
terms.description: An authoritative entity, represented by a public key and associated data, that serves as a root of trust for validating certificates and attestations.

terms.name: Trusted List
terms.description: A list providing the status and status history of trust services from trust service providers regarding compliance with applicable requirements (ETSI TS 119 612).

terms.name: Type
terms.description: Wallet type: designed for individual users (personal) or for organizations to manage credentials (organizational).

terms.name: UN Transparency Protocol
terms.description: A UN/CEFACT standard (UNTP) for interoperable digital credentials and discovery mechanisms that enable verifiable supply chain transparency at scale without a central data store.

terms.name: UN/CEFACT
terms.description: UN/CEFACT and related trade and supply-chain data exchange contexts, including the UN Transparency Protocol (UNTP) and cross-border trade credentials.

terms.name: UN/CEFACT
terms.description: United Nations Centre for Trade Facilitation and Electronic Business; develops standards for cross-border trade data exchange, including the UN Transparency Protocol (UNTP).

terms.name: Unique Identification Authority of India
terms.description: The Indian government authority responsible for the Aadhaar identity system and related digital identity credentials.

terms.name: UNTP Core Vocabulary
terms.description: The shared UNTP linked-data vocabulary of classes and properties (such as Product, Facility, Party, and Claim) reused across all UNTP credential types for consistent semantics.

terms.name: VC Format
terms.description: The technical format in which credentials are encoded. Different formats support different features like selective disclosure, privacy protection, or compatibility with specific standards.

terms.name: VC-JOSE-COSE
terms.description: W3C specification for securing verifiable credentials using JSON Web Signature/Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE).
aliases: Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE

terms.name: VCDM 1.1
terms.description: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 1.1, commonly carried as JWT VC.

terms.name: VCDM 2.0
terms.description: W3C standard data model for expressing verifiable credentials in a secure, privacy-respecting way.

terms.name: VCDM 2.0
terms.description: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0, including JSON-LD and related proof formats.

terms.name: Vehicle Registration Certificate
terms.description: An ISO mobile document credential attesting vehicle registration details, carried as an MSO mdoc (mVRC).

terms.name: Verifiable Credential
terms.description: A tamper-evident credential whose authorship (issuer) can be cryptographically verified.

terms.name: Verifiable Credential Data Integrity
terms.description: W3C specification defining data integrity proofs for verifiable credentials, including proof types used with JSON-LD and related VC 2.0 securing mechanisms.

terms.name: Verifiable Credential Type
terms.description: A string identifier (vct) in SD-JWT VC metadata that names the credential type and links to its schema, commonly used in EU and EWC attestation catalogs.

terms.name: Verifiable Credentials Data Model
terms.description: The W3C data model for expressing verifiable credentials; an umbrella term covering versions 1.1 and 2.0.

terms.name: Verifiable Credentials Profile
terms.description: The UNTP profile specifying W3C Verifiable Credentials and DID standards that underpin all UNTP credentials, ensuring they are signed, tamper-evident, revocable, and independently verifiable.

terms.name: verifiable LEI
terms.description: A digitally verifiable representation of a Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) and related organizational roles, issued under the GLEIF vLEI ecosystem using ACDC credentials.

terms.name: Verifiable Presentation
terms.description: A tamper-evident presentation of one or more credentials that a holder shares with a verifier, with cryptographic proof of provenance.

terms.name: Verifier
terms.description: Can request and verify credentials presented by holders (verifier role).

terms.name: vLEI
terms.description: GLEIF verifiable Legal Entity Identifier ecosystem using ACDC credentials to represent organizations, roles, and engagement context.

terms.name: vLEI Legal Entity Credential
terms.description: A vLEI credential issued to a legal entity, providing a verifiable digital representation of the organization based on its LEI.

terms.key: W3C Verifiable Credentials Status List v2021
terms.name: W3C Verifiable Credentials Status List v2021
terms.description: Standard status list format for checking revocation and suspension of W3C credentials.

terms.name: Wallet
terms.description: The digital equivalent of a physical wallet. A wallet enables a person or organization to securely store, manage, receive, present, and use digital identities, credentials, certificates, documents, payment instruments, digital currencies, and other digital assets.

terms.name: Wallet Instance
terms.description: The application installed and configured on a user's device or environment that the user interacts with; part of a Wallet Unit. Can also be a web application.

terms.name: Wallet Instance Attestation
terms.description: A type of Wallet Unit Attestation that attests the integrity and authenticity of a Wallet Instance and carries information about the Wallet Solution.

terms.name: Wallet Provider
terms.description: A natural or legal person who provides Wallet Solutions in the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

terms.name: Wallet Relying Party Repository
terms.description: A repository defined under the eIDAS 2.0 European Digital Identity Wallet framework that provides trusted information about relying parties, including their identifiers, authorizations and service metadata. EUDI Wallets can use the repository to validate relying parties and inform users before data is shared.

terms.name: Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application
terms.description: An application that manages critical assets by using the cryptographic and non-cryptographic functions provided by the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device.

terms.name: Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device
terms.description: A tamper-resistant device that protects critical assets and provides cryptographic functions for the secure execution of critical operations in a Wallet Unit.

terms.name: Wallet Solution
terms.description: The combination of software, hardware, services, settings and configurations (including Wallet Instances, WSCAs and WSCDs) that makes up a wallet product.

terms.name: Wallet Unit
terms.description: A unique configuration of a Wallet Solution, including Wallet Instances and the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Applications and Devices, provided by a Wallet Provider to an individual user.

terms.name: Wallet Unit Attestation
terms.description: A data object that describes the components of a Wallet Unit or allows authentication and validation of those components.

terms.name: WE BUILD
terms.description: Wallet Ecosystem for Business and payments Use cases on Identification, Legal representation and Data sharing: an EU Large Scale Pilot consortium testing European Business Wallet and EUDI Wallet business, supply-chain and payment use cases.

terms.name: Web Authentication
terms.description: W3C API for strong user authentication with public-key credentials; referenced in EUDI Wallet user authentication and device binding requirements.

terms.name: X.509 Certificate
terms.description: PKI certificate binding an identity to a public key; enables trust through established certificate chains.

terms.name: XAdES
terms.description: XML Advanced Electronic Signatures; ETSI baseline format for signing XML documents (ETSI EN 319 132-1).

terms.name: Zero-Knowledge Proof
terms.description: A cryptographic method that proves a statement is true without revealing the underlying data (for example proving age over 18 without revealing the birth date).
